text:
anya: quick heads-up from the shard reassign test - after a handful of handoffs a subset of prefixes stay "sticky" in the evict queue and never reach terminal state. memory for those prefix entries climbs and p95 tail tokens spike. debug logs attached.

devon: can you paste the most relevant trace?

anya: sure, small excerpt:
```
[handoff] claim shard=17 -> ok epoch=402
[handoff] transfer prefix=org/42/foo lease_release -> ack_sent
[evict] enqueue prefix=org/42/foo token=0x10ff -> ENQUEUED
[handoff] release_ack prefix=org/42/foo from=old-node -> drop (old epoch)
[evict] dequeue prefix=org/42/foo -> not-found (coord hash mismatch)
```
This sequence repeats for some keys where the coordinator loses the mapping between the queue entry and the new shard owner.

li: hmm looks like a timing window where release_ack from the old owner is dropped because it's from the previous epoch, but the enqueue used the old owner id in the coordinator index. When the new owner tries to dequeue it can't find the entry under its shard key. So entry becomes orphaned.

teja: two orthogonal fixes: 1) Keep queue entries indexed by a stable logical prefix key (prefix + monotonic enqueue-id) instead of owner-specific shard key. That makes dequeues owner-agnostic. 2) Add an ack-ledger: when a handoff completes, coordinator writes a short-lived ledger entry mapping enqueue-id -> owner-epoch; dequeue consults ledger to locate the entry. Ledger needs GC.

devon: option 1 seems simpler and cheaper runtime-wise: stable keys + a small indirection table so we don't need owner-bound indices. But we need to ensure dedupe and idempotency still hold when old owner retries.

anya: dedupe today is weak: we check an in-memory set per coordinator node. With stable enqueue-ids we'd switch to _global_ dedupe by storing enqueue-id in the queue record and making enqueue a compare-and-set on the queue's primary index. That removes duplicate enqueue ambiguity across epochs.

indra: ledger approach has an advantage for rollout: we can implement ledger as a small RAFT-backed table and migrate entries gradually. But adds cross-node state. Also need to think about GC / retention and how to recover if ledger loses entries (we'll need to tolerate orphans).

li: another idea: optimistic background reaper. Periodically scan queue for entries unreachable from any owner mapping and attempt to either route them to the new owner or mark them for TTL-based eviction. This is resilient but could be noisy and expensive at large scale.

teja: tradeoffs summary: stable-key approach: +simple, cheap, no extra cross-node state; -requires primary index change and row-level CAS on enqueue which may hurt enqueue latency slightly. Ledger: +easier owner lookup, incremental migration; -extra distributed state and GC complexity. Reaper: +no critical-path changes; -eventual, heavy scans.

anya: for the short-term mitigation I'm going to: 1) add a conservative reaper job with a low rate and heuristics to only touch prefixes with >2 handoffs in the last 30s; 2) add a per-node metric orphaned_queue_entries; 3) flip a feature flag to enable stable-key enqueue on a single canary node to collect perf numbers.

devon: SGTM. make sure to include enqueue latency and enqueue error rate dashboards when we test stable-key. Also add an enrichment tag on queue rows with enqueue-origin-epoch so we can validate behavior during handoffs.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started: stable-enqueue-key.v1 -> canary-1 at 2026-03-23T17:12:00Z

li: long-term I'd prefer the stable-key model + a small shard-index indirection for fast owner lookup. That lets dequeue be O(1) and keeps the queue compact. We'll need a migration plan: backfill existing queue rows with enqueue-ids and rewrite index to new key atomically (or via dual-write window).

teja: migration sketch: dual-write for 5m after rollout, then backfill leftover rows using a background rewriter that tags old rows with enqueue-ids. After backfill we flip to the new primary key. Plan must include pause-enqueue mode for short window in case of issues.

anya: also thinking about tombstone semantics: when a prefix is deleted mid-handoff, we should allow a tombstone message to short-circuit regardless of epoch. But we must avoid a tombstone from an old epoch resurrecting a prefix on another owner. Proposal: tombstone messages carry (tombstone=true, tombstone-epoch) and dequeue applies tombstone iff tombstone-epoch >= enqueue-origin-epoch. That ensures freshness.

indra: good. also add a tombstone-ttl to guard against accidental permanent tombstones if GC fails.

devon: ops checklist for canary: metrics (orphaned_queue_entries, enqueue_latency_ms_p95, enqueue_cas_conflicts), feature flag, rollback steps (disable stable-key, accelerate reaper, drain canary queue), postmortem trigger if orphaned entries > 1000 for >10m.

anya: I'll open a PR with the canary changes + smoke tests (handoff storm sim, tombstone race). tagging reviewers. :rocket:

ops-bot: Canary rollout healthy: stable-enqueue-key.v1 on canary-1 (ok).

li: after canary, schedule a multi-node chaos run that simulates concurrent handoffs and node flaps. We should validate the reaper doesn't over-eagerly delete entries.

teja: note for RFC: include benchmarks for enqueue CAS versus current weak dedupe, cost model (index storage growth), and migration steps. Also a small prototype of the backfill rewriter code.

anya: thanks everyone. I'll document the migration steps and schedule the chaos run next week. :thumbsup:
